title: Alzer–Qiu's monotonicity and convexity conjecture for the elliptic-integral ratio
statement:
Let $\mathscr{K}(r)$ denote the complete elliptic integral of the first kind for $r\in(0,1)$, and define

$$
G(r)=\frac{\log(2\mathscr{K}(r)/\pi)}{\log((\operatorname{arth} r)/r)}.
$$

**Alzer–Qiu's conjecture.** The function $G$ is strictly increasing and convex from $(0,1)$ onto $(3/4,1)$.

This conjecture refines the best possible exponents in bounds approximating the complete elliptic integral by $(\operatorname{arth} r)/r$. The source notes that the conjecture remained difficult to prove; no resolution is supplied here.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.04072

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021).
source_name: Song-Liang Qiu, Qi Bao, Xiao-Yan Ma and Hong-Biao Jiang, “On a Conjecture Concerning the Approximates of Complete Elliptic Integral of the First Kind by Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent”, arXiv:2103.04072 (2021).
